name: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct
notes: TWO-PART MODEL. (1) Vision: 32-layer ViT, hidden 1280, 16 heads, patch 14, spatial_merge 2, out_hidden_size 3584 -- same shape as Qwen2-VL but with WINDOWED attention (window_size 112 px) and only 4 full-attention blocks at depths [7,15,23,31]. Windowing makes encoder cost near-linear in patch count instead of quadratic, which is what makes high-resolution input affordable. (2) LLM: Qwen2-7B dense decoder, identical dims to Qwen2-VL (28 layers, 28 heads / 4 KV, head_dim 128; k_proj [512,3584] confirms). ARCHITECTURE = dense. CONTEXT_SCALING = mrope, mrope_section [16,24,24], rope_theta 1e6. Unusual scheme: temporal and height position indices are interleaved into the same head-dim halves as width, so video and multi-image prompts stay positionally distinguishable. VISION TOKENS: preprocessor_config sets min_pixels 3,136 and max_pixels 12,845,056 with patch 14 / merge 2, so tokens = pixels / (28*28) = pixels / 784. Bounds: 4 tokens minimum, 16,384 tokens maximum. A 448x448 image = 256 tokens. DOMINANCE: at the default 1024x1024 (1,049,576 px) the image yields 1,339 vision tokens, which outnumbers a typical ~300-token text prompt ~4:1. VISION DOMINATES PREFILL for Qwen2.5-VL at any resolution above roughly 600x600. That is the single most decision-relevant fact about this model. KV CACHE: 28 * 4 * 128 * 2 * 2 = 57,344 B/token. At the 128,000 max_position_embeddings that is 7.0 GiB resident KV per sequence at bf16 -- the 4x context increase over Qwen2-VL is a 4x memory commitment, not a free upgrade. params_b 8.292 = HF API safetensors total (8,292,166,656).
